LK1 re-sequenced

260522_VH01624_461_222JLJVNX

2026-08-03

Run: 260522_VH01624_461_222JLJVNX (re-sequencing of 260423_VH01624_453_222HWMYNX)

Status: current. This is the LK1 data used by all later analyses; the pilot run 260423_VH01624_453_222HWMYNX it replaces is superseded.

Analysis finished: 2026-06-01 - the most recent of the 13 figures shown below.

Report generated: 2026-08-03 by 05.LK1_resequenced_report.Rmd, from the outputs of steps 01-04 in this folder.

LK1 was sequenced a second time to decide whether the pilot depth was sufficient, and whether the rest of the cohort needed deeper sequencing. The comparison is against the pilot run and against the published AML scAtlas.

For full report, download LK1_resequenced_report.html in the attachment and open in a browser.

Code used - attached and in the github repository: https://github.com/nbartonicek/surface_proteome_dev/tree/main/lab_archives/LK1-resequenced

Aim

Identify whether we are getting a comparable amount of key features to the AML scAtlas - cells, genes and UMIs - and evaluate whether further sequencing is required, via:

  • subsampling of reads
  • differential expression between cell types
  • separation of clusters

Conclusions

  • AML scAtlas basic QC stats are comparable to our dataset, on average lower
  • subsampling of reads shows that we have reached saturation levels for cell detection
  • we have not reached saturation levels for: number of genes detected; number of UMIs per gene; number of DE genes for cells with either low (T-cells) or high (HSCs) numbers of genes expressed
  • cluster separation of HSCs from other precursors (MEP) is slightly better for re-sequenced data
  • re-sequencing gained about 25% more genes and 39% more UMIs per cell for essentially no extra cells, which is the expected shape when a library is under-sequenced rather than under-loaded

1. What re-sequencing gained

First run vs re-sequenced, per-cell gain
name first_run resequenced absolute_gain fold_gain
median_genes 2052.000 2562.000 510.0000 1.248538
median_UMI 4202.000 5833.000 1631.0000 1.388149
mean_genes 2595.986 3095.429 499.4427 1.192390
mean_UMI 8396.377 11630.430 3234.0527 1.385172
Our two runs against the AML scAtlas
dataset cells median_genes mean_genes p10_genes p90_genes median_UMI mean_UMI p10_UMI p90_UMI
AML scAtlas 748679 1611 1801.281 690 3228 2195.882 2158.776 1448.527 2829.167
first_run 23133 2052 2595.986 920 5539 4202.000 8396.377 1479.000 24312.400
resequenced 23569 2562 3095.429 1115 6393 5833.000 11630.430 1892.800 34087.000

Cell numbers barely move while genes and UMIs per cell rise by a quarter and a third respectively. That is the signature of a library that was sequenced too shallowly rather than loaded too lightly - more reads recover more of the transcriptome from the cells already captured, rather than finding new cells.

Both runs sit above the atlas medians on genes and UMIs per cell, which is what “atlas stats are on average lower” in the conclusions refers to.

3. Saturation curves

Cell Ranger’s molecule-level downsampling, re-analysed at each depth and plotted against the atlas. These are the figures the saturation conclusions rest on.

curve_cells_detected_vs_AML.pdf

Cells detected vs depth - this one has plateaued. Extra reads do not recover extra cells.

curve_genes_per_cell_vs_AML.pdf

Genes per cell vs depth - still climbing. No plateau, so more depth would still add genes.

UMIs per gene vs depth - still climbing.

UMIs per cell vs depth.

Reads per cell across the depth series.

4. Effect of depth on downstream analysis

Two things were checked beyond raw counts: whether differential expression between cell types holds up at lower depth, and whether clusters still separate.

Cluster counts across the depth series, from the analysis in step 07 (reproduced from the read-depth deck, as the figure itself is not among the saved outputs):

Depth Total clusters HSC clusters
10% subsample 5 2
30% subsample 8 3
60% subsample (~pilot 1) 8 4
Full dataset 9 4

The full dataset resolves one cluster the 60% subsample does not - naive T-cells - and HSC separation from other precursors improves with depth. The pilot run sits at roughly the 60% point of the re-sequenced data, which is why its HSC/MEP separation is the weaker of the two.

6. What was run, in order

Step Script What it does
01 01.cellranger_resequence.sh Cell Ranger 10.0.0 count on the re-sequenced LK1 GEX library.
02 02.investigate_resequencing.R First run vs re-sequenced: cells, genes, UMIs, and the gain summary.
03 03.subsampling_vs_atlas.R Our depth against the AML scAtlas, plus the molecule-level saturation curves.
04 04.DE_subsampling.R Pseudobulk DE at each depth, then cluster HBDN501-AML-KMT2A and score separation.
05 05.LK1_resequenced_report.Rmd This report.

Each analysis appears once. Where a script went through successive revisions, the version kept is the one that produced the outputs shown, and its header names the revisions it supersedes:

8. Caveats

  1. The depth series here is Cell Ranger’s molecule-level downsampling, not a FASTQ-level re-run. The seqtk FASTQ downsampling with frac_000 to frac_090 directories is a separate, later exercise carried out on LK2 (cellranger_downsampled_reseq/260528…, 2026-06-15) and does not belong to this report.
  2. Step 05 hardcodes a downsampled path under this run that does not exist (cellranger_downsampled_reseq/260522…); only the LK2 equivalent is on disk. It runs against the molecule-level outputs regardless, but the path should be corrected before the script is reused.
  3. The cluster-count table in section 4 is taken from the read-depth deck; the figure behind it is not among the saved outputs.
